The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-
with interest for the death of Subramanya S/o. Late Lakshmanappa in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15-06-2024.
2.

The case of the petitioners in brief is as under:
SCCH-10 That, on 15.06.2024 at about 8.45 a.m., one Subramanya was proceeding in the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-15-U-3102 as a pillion rider and the same was ridden by one Mr.Vijayakumar slowly and cautiously on Shiralkoppa - Ulavi Tar Road, Patresalu Village, Shivamogga District, at that time, the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No. KL-60-C-6090 came from opposite direction at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the said Subramanya who was proceeding in the said motor cycle fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the son and petitioner No.3 is the mother of deceased and they are the legal heirs of deceased.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 28 years and he was self employed and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners are put to mental shock and agony and also lost their bread earner of the family.

Further, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver SCCH-10 of the Pooja vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137634729/
2 Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No.KL-60-C-6090.
As such, the respondent No.1 being insurer and respondent No.2 being owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents under all heads together with interest and costs.
3. In response to the Petition notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the Court through their respective counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The contentions of the respondent No.1 in brief are as under:
The respondent No.1 contended that, the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
Further denied the entire petition averments.
Further contended that, the accident is head on collusion.

The said motor cycle was not having insurance and the rider and the pillion rider were not wearing helmet, for that on 05.09.2024 the police imposed SCCH-10 penalty of Rs.1,500/- to the owner of said motor cycle.
The alleged accident caused due to rash and negligent riding on the part of rider of said motor cycle and negligence on the part of pillion rider.

Since the motor cycle was not having policy, to get compensation, the petitioners have filed a false case against the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg.
No.KL-60-C-6090.
Contributory negligence is more on the part of rider and pillion rider and if both were careful and vigilant, they could have avoided the accident.
Further, the respondent No.1 has denied for having issued insurance policy in respect of the offending tipper lorry as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and fanciful.
On all these main contentions, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

5. The contentions of the respondent No.2 in brief are as under:
The respondent No.2 contended that, the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on SCCH-10 facts of the case.

Further contended that,
the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary party as the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg. No.KL-60-C-6090 is not made as a party in this case.
Further denied the entire petitioner averments.

Further contended that, the driver of the Tipper lorry was possessed valid and effective driving licence and this respondent has made insurance to the said vehicle with the respondent No.1 and as such if the petitioners are entitled to claim the compensation, the respondent No.1 insurance company is liable to pay the same.
On all these main contentions, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against him.

 R E A S O N S 10. ISSUE No.1:
The petitioners have filed the present petition seeking SCCH-10 compensation on account of death of Subramanya in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15-06-2024.

11. According to the petitioners, deceased Subramanya was proceeding in the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-15- U-3102 as a pillion rider and the same was ridden by one Mr. Vijayakumar, at that time the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No. KL-60-C-6090 came from opposite direction at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle and as a result,
the deceased who was proceeding in the said motor cycle fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.

sentences.text: To substantiate the said contentions, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.
P.12. Ex.P.1 is the FIR in crime No.0068/2024 of Soraba PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 it reveal that, I.O. has registered a case against the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No.KL-60-C-6090 for the commission of offences punishable under Section 279 and SCCH-10 304-A of IPC and Section 187 of MV Act.
Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet filed by the Soraba police against one Mr. Mohan who is none other than the driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.8 are the Postmortem report and Inquest mahazar respectively.
On perusal of postmortem report, it reveals that the deceased died due to extra dural hematoma secondary to head injury in the accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and deceased succumbed to the injuries due to the accident.
13. The respondent No.1 has seriously disputed the negligent driving of driver of the vehicle.
According to the them, it is a head on collusion accident between the motor cycle and a tipper lorry and the rider of the motor cycle is also contributed to the accident.

It is specifically contended by the respondent No.1 that at the time of accident b oth the rider and pillion rider of the motor cycle were not wearing helmet and the motor cycle was not having valid insurance SCCH-10 on the date of accident.

On this ground, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has vehemently argued that the tipper lorry was falsely implicated for unlawful gain and the non wearing helmet by the deceased / pillion rider has also contributed for the cause of alleged accident.

The learned counsel for the respondent NO.1 has turned my attention toward copy of the challan to show that the owner of the motor cycle has paid penalty of Rs.1,500/- for not possessing valid insurance policy to the motor cycle and for not wearing helmet.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the non wearing of helmet cannot be considered for the purpose of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

The learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that Hon'ble Apex Court in catena of decisions held that, unless it is established that, the act of the rider of the motor cycle contributed to the accident or to the impact of the accident it cannot be held that,
there is a contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.

In the instant case,
even if it is assumed that, both the rider and the pillion rider were not SCCH-10 wearing helmet at the time of accident that cannot be considered as the negligent act on the part of the rider of the motor cycle for the cause of alleged accident.
Therefore, the argument canvassed by the respondent No.1 that the rider and pillion rider of the motor cycle have also contributed for the cause of accident holds no water.
Further, in the charge sheet I.O. has not stated anything regarding the negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle in causing the accident.
14. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

In this view, Court receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.
15.

Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:-
It is the contention of the petitioners that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the son and petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased.
In order to prove the relationship with the deceased, the petitioners have produced copies of Aadhaar cards as per Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12.
On perusal of Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12 it reveal that, the petitioners are the wife, son and mother of deceased.
Further, the respondents have not so seriously disputed the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

Hence,
I hold that the petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.3:
It is the specific contention of the petitioners that, deceased Subramanya was hale and healthy at the time of SCCH-10 accident and was a self employed and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to untimely death of deceased they put to great hardship and lost their bread earner of the family.
18. To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have produced the Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9, the date of birth of Subramanya is shown as 01.01.1992.
The accident was occurred on 01.01.2024.
Therefore, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged 32 years.
19. Further, to prove the occupation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any document.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - SCCH-10 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, if the accident occurred in the year 2022, the notional income has to be taken as Rs.15,500/- per month.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the deceased would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 15.06.2024.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,500/- as monthly income of the deceased.

20. Before proceeding to award compensation under the different heads, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in Special Leave Petition (Civil)

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Apex Court in para No.61 has proceeded to record the following conclusions;
(iv) In case the deceased was self- employed or on fixed salary, an addition SCCH-10 of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

(v) For determination of the multiplicand, the deduction for personal and living expenses, the tribunals and the courts shall be guided by paragraphs 30 to 32 of Sarla Verma which we have reproduced hereinbefore.
(vi) The selection of multiplier shall be as indicated in the Table in Sarla Verma read with paragraph 42 of that judgment.
(vii) The age of the deceased should be the basis for applying the multiplier.
(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional head, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
21. As per the records, at the time of accident the deceased was aged 32 years.
Further, there is no dispute regarding the age of the deceased.
Hence, the age of the deceased is taken as 32 years at the time of accident for SCCH-10 multiplier.

As per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 an operative multiplier of 16 is applicable for the age group of 31 to 35 years.

sentences.text: 22. In the instant case, the deceased left behind his wife, son and mother and they are dependents of the deceased.

In Sarla Verma case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has expressed the view regarding standardized deduction towards personal and living expenses, where the number of dependents are 2 to 3, the deduction would be 1/3 rd.

As discussed supra, in the present case, claimant No.1 (wife),
Claimant No.2 (minor son) and claimant No.3 (mother) of the deceased are the dependents.

Hence,
in the present case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
In the present case, the Court has taken the view that the deceased was having monthly income of Rs.16,500/- and annual income would be Rs.1,98,000/-.
If 1/3 rd is deducted towards personal expenses, the contribution to the family (dependents) is determined as Rs.1,32,000/-.

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi case, if the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was under the age group of below 40 years.
In the present case, the deceased was aged 32 years at the time of accident and was on fixed salary.
Hence, an addition of 40% shall be added to Rs.1,32,000/-, it would be Rs.1,84,800/-.
The multiplier will be 16 having regard to the age of the deceased at the time of death (32 years).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,84,800/- X 16 = Rs.29,56,800/-.
Thus, Rs.29,56,800/- is the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

24. As per Pranay Sethi Case, reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years from the date of judgment (31.10.2017).
Therefore, in the instant case, the petitioners are entitled for the aforesaid SCCH-10 conventional heads with enhanced rate of 20%.

sentences.text: REGARDING LIABILITY:
As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg. No.KL-60-C-6090.
The respondent No.2 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.1, as such, respondent No.1 has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.
Hence, the respondents No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

The respondent No.2 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation of Rs.31,36,800/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the SCCH-10 date of petition till the date of realization in the ratio of 40:35:25 respectively.

Accordingly,
I answer the issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.4:
29.

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.31,36,800/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled to receive compensation in the ratio of 40:35:25 respectively from the Respondent No.1 Insurance company.

The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988.

Out of the award amount, 40% of the award SCCH-10 amount of petitioner No.1 and 3 shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank of petitioners' choice and balance amount shall be released to them through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The entire compensation amount awarded to the petitioner No.2, shall be invested in fixed deposit in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice till he attain the age of majority.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
